plotSections.title: Keystone Keepers Chosen
bullets: Walker chooses The Reach rather than La-rel, explaining that although La-rel was an important part of his past, he no longer feels it represents who he is; Glimmen supports either choice.
Dana accepts the Pitel keystone and becomes its protector, describing Pitel as the center of the rings of Atlas.
Ord chooses Feldspar, the realm associated with magic, science, and alchemy.
Ciri chooses Lith, despite its people having sworn off magic; Lith's people instead understand supernatural phenomena through folklore, fairy tales, cryptids, and legends.
The party is now established as the keepers of six keystones: Gerk/Midgard, Sylan/Gilbrick, Dana/Pitel, Walker/The Reach, Ord/Feldspar, and Ciri/Lith.

plotSections.title: The Unchosen Keystones
bullets: Two of the eight keystones remain unchosen: La-rel and Turof.
These two keystones will remain under the stewardship of Kit Anger and the DM's character until two future keepers can take up their mantles.
The remaining keystones should not be forgotten; the current stewards promise to protect them until new keepers can be found.

plotSections.title: Children of the Great Eldarin Tree
bullets: The party's acceptance of the keystones makes them keepers and connects them to the Children of the Great Eldarin Tree.
The keystones are powerful objects that require great care, and the party is now responsible for protecting them from falling into the wrong hands.

The party's new responsibilities create an apparent reversal: they originally sought a lich who was pursuing these powerful objects, but they have now been entrusted with protecting the very things the lich seeks.

plotSections.title: The Lich and the Party's New Responsibility
bullets: The party has repeatedly sought ways to find or become safer from the lich who is pursuing the keystones.
The current situation may instead make the party more directly involved, since they have now been entrusted with protecting the keystones.
The party is urged to protect the keystones and not allow them to fall, while recognizing that events may be driven by fate beyond the speaker's control.
The keeper role gives the party greater status and responsibility, with the implications of Gerk's new mantle beginning to be revealed at the end of the conversation.

chronologicalEvents: Walker decides that The Reach is more appropriate for him now than La-rel, because La-rel represents an important part of his past rather than who he currently is.
Glimmen tells Walker that home is where they make it and says she is comfortable with either choice.
Walker receives the keystone for The Reach. The Reach is described as the largest of the arches, with extensive territory that Walker and Glimmen should be able to traverse efficiently.
Dana is offered the Pitel keystone because of her previous interest in reaching Pitel and accepts it, declaring that she is honored to guard the center of the rings of Atlas.
The remaining available keystones are identified as Feldspar, La-rel, Turof, and Lith.
Ord is offered a choice between the remaining keystones and chooses Feldspar, attracted to its combination of magic, science, and alchemy.
Feldspar is described as a realm involving magic, science, and unusual alchemical experimentation.
Lith is clarified as a realm whose people have sworn off magic but still encounter supernatural phenomena, interpreting them as folklore, fairy tales, cryptids, and legends.
Ciri returns and is told that she must choose one of the remaining keystones.
Ciri is offered La-rel, Turof, or Lith and chooses Lith.
La-rel is identified as the realm of fairies, also called the Feywilds, and Renard is recalled as the smiling trickster the party encountered there.
The party confirms that they have previously visited La-rel but have not knowingly visited Turof or Lith.
The DM explains that Lith's people may call Ciri a witch if she uses magic, but she will nevertheless become part of their history and may have holidays named after her.
The party recognizes that there are eight keystones but only six current keepers.
La-rel and Turof remain unchosen and will be watched over by Kit Anger and the DM's character as stewards until future keepers can take up the mantles.
The party is formally described as keepers of the keystones and as Children of the Great Eldarin Tree.
The DM points out the irony that the party has been searching for a lich pursuing the keystones, while the party has now been entrusted with protecting those same objects.
The party is warned that the keystones are powerful and require great care in how they are used.
The DM begins explaining that Gerk's new mantle makes him more than he was before, but the transcript ends before the explanation is completed.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter; Glimmen is his mind-linked dragon.
notes: Chooses The Reach as his keystone realm rather than La-rel.
Walker feels that La-rel represents an important part of his past but no longer represents who he is.
Glimmen supports either choice and emphasizes that home is where they make it.
Walker and Glimmen are considered particularly well suited to traveling the vast Reach because of their ability to fly.
personality: Walker is reflective about how his identity has changed since his earlier experiences in La-rel.
quotesThemes: The Reach feels more appropriate to who Walker is now than La-rel.

notes: Glimmen tells Walker that home is where they make it.
Glimmen is comfortable with either La-rel or The Reach as Walker's chosen realm.
Glimmen and Walker are expected to be able to travel the large Reach with relative ease.
personality: Reflective about the contrast between her earlier experiences and her current life.
quotesThemes: Home is where we make it.

The Reach.existing: One of the arches/realms of Atlas.
notes: Walker chooses The Reach as the realm he will protect.
The Reach is described as the biggest of the arches.
Its size makes extensive exploration possible, but Walker and Glimmen's ability to fly should make traversing it easier.

Dana.existing: Half-elf cleric and the most knowledgeable member of the group.
notes: Accepts the Pitel keystone and agrees to protect Pitel.
Describes her responsibility as guarding the center of the rings of Atlas.
Her prior desire to find a way to reach Pitel is referenced when the keystone is offered.
personality: Treats the responsibility of guarding Pitel as a great honor.
quotesThemes: Dana is honored to guard the center of the rings of Atlas.

Pitel.existing: An arch/realm of Atlas located at the center of the rings of Atlas.
notes: Dana becomes the keeper of Pitel.
Pitel is described as the center or core of the rings of Atlas.
Dana had previously sought a way to reach Pitel, apparently in connection with the realm's unusual relationship to time.
titles: Center of the rings of Atlas

notes: Chooses Feldspar as the realm he will protect.
Ord specifically favors Feldspar because of its combination of magic and science.
personality: Interested in the combination of magic, science, and alchemy.

Feldspar.existing: One of the arches/realms of Atlas.
notes: Ord becomes the keeper of Feldspar.
Feldspar is associated with magic, science, and alchemical experimentation.
It is described as the second-most inner sanctum of knowledge, magic, and alchemical experiments.
titles: Second-most inner sanctum of knowledge, magic, and alchemical experiments

notes: Chooses Lith as the realm she will protect.
Ciri had not previously visited Lith or Turof, though the party has visited La-rel.
Her use of magic in Lith may cause its people to interpret her as a witch, but she is expected to become part of their history and folklore.

Lith.existing: One of the arches/realms of Atlas; its people have sworn off magic.
notes: Ciri becomes the keeper of Lith.
Lith's inhabitants have sworn off magic but are not ignorant; they understand supernatural phenomena through stories, folklore, fairy tales, and cryptids.
Events or beings from other worlds can occasionally appear in Lith and frighten its inhabitants, becoming the basis for new legends and cryptids.
The people of Lith may interpret Ciri's magic as witchcraft.
Ciri is expected to become an important historical and folkloric figure in Lith.
quotesThemes: Lith's people interpret supernatural phenomena as folklore and legends because they are distant from the underlying truth.

La-rel.existing: One of the arches/realms of Atlas; the realm of fairies, also called the Feywilds.
notes: Walker considers La-rel but ultimately decides The Reach is more appropriate for him.
The party has previously visited La-rel.
Renard, the smiling trickster, was encountered there.
La-rel is one of the two currently unchosen keystone realms.

Turof.existing: One of the arches/realms of Atlas.
notes: Turof remains one of the two unchosen keystone realms.
The party has not knowingly visited Turof.

Renard.existing: Smiling trickster encountered by the party in La-rel.
notes: Ciri and the DM recall Renard when discussing the party's previous visit to La-rel.
Will serve as one of the stewards responsible for the unchosen La-rel and Turof keystones.

Great Eldarin Tree.existing: Sacred origin associated with the keystones and the Navi.
notes: The party is explicitly described as Children of the Great Eldarin Tree after taking on the keeper mantles.
The keeper role is presented as a continuation of the party's efforts to protect and recover the keystones.
quotesThemes: The party is now considered children of the Great Eldarin Tree and keepers of the keystones.

notes: The six party members now each hold and protect one keystone.
Current assignments are Gerk/Midgard, Sylan/Gilbrick, Dana/Pitel, Walker/The Reach, Ord/Feldspar, and Ciri/Lith.
The keepers are responsible for protecting the powerful keystones and preventing them from falling into the wrong hands.
titles: Children of the Great Eldarin Tree

notes: Gerk is confirmed as having chosen Midgard as the realm he will protect.
The DM begins explaining that taking on the keeper mantle makes Gerk more than he was previously, but the transcript ends before the explanation is completed.
openQuestions: What exactly does Gerk become by taking on the keeper mantle?

newTerms.name: Keeper of the Keystone
notes: A mantle held by the party members who have accepted responsibility for protecting one of the keystones and its associated realm.

newTerms.name: Children of the Great Eldarin Tree
notes: The party is now described as Children of the Great Eldarin Tree as a consequence of taking on the keeper mantles.

newTerms.name: Stewards of the Unchosen Keystones
notes: Kit Anger and the DM's character will temporarily safeguard the La-rel and Turof keystones until future keepers can take up their mantles.

newTerms.name: Lith Folklore
notes: Lith's people have rejected conventional magic but still encounter supernatural phenomena, interpreting them through folklore, fairy tales, cryptids, and legends.
